difficulty_calibration.notes: This sits at the 'Extreme' end of the ESAT spectrum because it requires a multi-stage proportional chain (Mass -> Radius -> Area -> Velocity). It is well-calibrated for high-performing candidates.

selectivity_audit.main_trap: The trap is the interplay between the cubic mass scaling and the quadratic area scaling, which forces the student to correctly identify the power-law relationship $v \propto m^{1/6}$.
selectivity_audit.why_not_plug_and_chug: There is no formula provided for terminal velocity in terms of mass and area; the student must construct the equilibrium condition $mg = kAv^2$ and derive the scaling factors from geometry.
selectivity_audit.expected_mid_student_error: Mid-tier students will likely fail to account for the area scaling (choosing D) or fail to correctly apply the square root to the final ratio (choosing C).

notes: Excellent use of proportional reasoning. The scaling factors (64, 4, 16, 2) are chosen perfectly for no-calculator mental arithmetic.
